extracted.intended_audience: general readers, prospective readers/subscribers, potential advertisers, and job applicants (journalists/industry professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational standards and principles for Semafor's journalism and advertising: how reporting is structured and labeled (the 'Semaform'), how diverse/global perspectives are presented and distilled, and rules governing advertising acceptance, labeling, and prohibited content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent News / Semaform structure
rubrics_metrics.description: “Exposing the architecture of our original journalism… Our ‘Semaform’ structure makes clear the lines between facts, analysis, opinion, counter-narratives, and global perspectives.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design reporting to reveal its underlying architecture so readers can see what is fact versus analysis or opinion; label and separate these elements explicitly to rebuild trust and increase transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distilled Views (pairing original reporting with curated perspectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Single sources can’t always capture the complexity of a story… Our original journalism will be paired with distilled news, analysis, and opinion from a global range of sources.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide smart, distilled summaries and curated perspectives alongside original reporting to cut through the news cycle; use distillation to surface diverse viewpoints and simplify complex, cross-border stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: “We’re a global news company at birth. We believe that informed citizens of every country need to understand what drives decisions, actions, culture and power beyond their own borders.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize coverage that situates events in transnational context and incorporates reporting and analysis from multiple countries and regions rather than a solely domestic viewpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray different points of view grounded in a singular set of facts
rubrics_metrics.description: “Our coverage seeks to portray different points of view across every story, grounded in a singular set of facts.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present competing perspectives and counter-narratives while clearly establishing and preserving a shared factual baseline for the story; ensure perspective pieces do not obscure agreed facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict separation between advertising and editorial
rubrics_metrics.description: “Our advertisers are a key force in supporting our newsroom but have no bearing on our editorial coverage, and we maintain a strict separation between news and third-party ads.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain editorial independence from commercial partners; ensure newsroom decisions and coverage priorities are made without advertiser influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open advertising space subject to review and rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: “To that end, our advertising space is open to all points of view – cultural, political, social and otherwise. Semafor reserves the right to review all ads and to reject any that are determined to be in violation of our principles and ad acceptability standards.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While advertising is broadly open to viewpoints, implement an ad review process with clear acceptability standards and authority to reject ads that conflict with organizational principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear presentation and transparency of advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: “Semafor will ensure that all advertising is clearly presented as commercial content, distinct from editorial content. The nature of an advertising relationship must be transparent so that it is clear to the audience that they are seeing a commercial message.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label ads prominently and make any commercial relationship transparent to readers; avoid formats that could blur the line between editorial content and advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited advertising content and legal compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: “Semafor prohibits advertising that promotes hate speech, discrimination, violence as well as advertising that knowingly misleads readers via fraudulence or inaccuracy or that violates federal or local stipulations protecting trademark, copyright, libel, stock involvement and political advertising.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject ads that contain hate speech, discrimination, incitement to violence, deliberate misinformation, or that infringe legal protections (trademark, copyright, libel); ensure ads comply with applicable laws and regulations, including rules on political advertising and securities-related claims.
